title: SLO declarations for bursty LLM routes and graceful eviction policy
creator: Maria Chen
description: Goal: Produce a concise, machine-parseable SLO declaration and operational policy for our high-throughput, bursty LLM routes (chat.generate, text.generate, embeddings) that ties SLIs to per-route/model error budgets, defines automated mitigation (circuit breakers + load-shedding), and specifies multi-region failover behavior. This ticket covers: 1) concrete SLI definitions per route and per model-variant (what to measure and how), 2) error budget burn windows and automated responses, 3) circuit breaker thresholds and states, 4) prioritized load-shedding / graceful eviction rules (including model fallback order), 5) mapping to owners and runbooks, and 6) monitoring + dashboards required for enforcement and async review. Background: We see bursty traffic patterns from several customers using chat.generate with spiky delta in token throughput. Current SLOs are route-level but not model-variant-aware; we lack a deterministic policy for when to degrade to cheaper quantized variants or shed less-critical routes during regional capacity stress. This ambiguity has caused late-night manual interventions and inconsistent customer experience. Proposed SLO/SLI approach: - SLI surface: success_rate (bool success = 2xx + streaming completed without early abort), latency_ms distribution, tail_latency_ms (p95/p99), token_success_rate (percentage of requests that finished vs aborted), and model_quality_regressions (eval-set BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim drift). - Per-route baseline SLOs: * chat.generate (interactive): availability = 99.95% monthly (success_rate), p95 latency <= 450ms for small contexts (< 512 tokens), p95 latency <= 900ms for long contexts (>=512 tokens). * text.generate (batch): availability = 99.9% monthly, p95 latency <= 1200ms. * embeddings: availability = 99.99% monthly, p99 latency <= 250ms. - Per-model variant adjustments: high-capacity variants (e.g., redwood-large) inherit route SLOs. Quantized/fast variants (e.g., redwood-fast-8bit) get relaxed latency SLOs (+30%) and reduced availability requirements if they are marked fallback-only. - Measurement window: rolling 30d for availability, 7d and 1d windows for alerting and burn-rate calculations. - Error budgeting and burn policy: monthly error budget = (1 - availability) * total requests for each route+model combination. Burn rate computed over 1h and 24h windows. Automated responses at burn thresholds: * burn_rate >= 4x over 1h OR remaining_budget <= 25%: enable conservative mitigations (soft shedding of best-effort routes, restrict rate-limits for guests, switch eligible traffic to quantized variant if model-quality delta < threshold). * burn_rate >= 8x over 1h OR remaining_budget <= 10%: enable aggressive mitigations (disable non-essential routes, enable global circuit breaker for affected model-variant, start regional failover policy). * remaining_budget == 0% sustained for 30m: trigger incident page, rollback recent runtime changes per changelog, and perform mandatory investigation. - Circuit breaker design: state machine = CLOSED -> HALF_OPEN -> OPEN. Triggers to OPEN: sustained error rate > 2% for 5 minutes OR queue length (requests waiting) > 95th historical percentile AND CPU/GPU utilization > 92% for 2m. When OPEN: route-level traffic diverted according to priority map (see load-shedding), fallback routing to compatible model variants if available. HALF_OPEN: allow 1% of traffic as probes with raised timeout; if probe success_rate > 99% over 10m, transition to CLOSED. Circuit breaker scope: per-model-variant per-region and a global umbrella breaker that aggregates regional health. - Load-shedding / graceful eviction: priority levels = critical (webhook callbacks, billing-related), high (interactive chat for paid customers), medium (background batch inference for async features), low (free-tier or experimental routes). Eviction order: low -> medium -> high -> critical. Eviction mechanisms: reduce concurrency cap, degrade max_tokens, switch to fast-quantized model variant, or return 503 with Retry-After for guest traffic. Ensure deterministic order and rate limits to avoid amplify thrashing. - Multi-region failover: active-active preferred for chat.generate with per-region SLOs. Failover triggers: persistent regional circuit breaker OPEN OR regional p95 latency > regional SLO * 1.5 for 10m. Failover strategy: gradual traffic shift via traffic manager (10% increments every 30s) with canary probes to ensure downstream model variants in target region satisfy SLIs. DNS TTLs must be <= 30s for rapid steering; control-plane safeguards to avoid split-brain. - Ownership and runbooks: runtime-sre: primary for breaker automation and escalation; model-serving: primary for model-variant fallback matrix and quality thresholds; platform-product: owns customer-facing communication templates when evictions occur. Add new runbooks: SLO-burn-automation.md, circuit-breaker-playbook.md, multi-region-failover-checklist.md and link in the resources. - Observability and dashboards: per-route+model SLI time-series, burn-rate charts (1h/24h), circuit-breaker status panel, per-region capacity heatmap, and a synthetic-probe matrix. Alerts: warn at remaining_budget <= 25% (P0->ops channel), page at remaining_budget <= 10% or circuit breaker OPEN. Implementation notes: - Produce a machine-readable SLO declaration (YAML/JSON) that the runtime controller can ingest. Schema should include route, model_variant, SLI metric names, SLO target, measurement windows, owner, fallback_order, and mitigation actions. - Add an API endpoint for querying active mitigation state and reasons for a given route+model. - Implement a feature-flagged rollout of automated mitigations for two pilot customers before wide enablement. - Provide a compatibility matrix that maps models to allowable fallback variants and an automated quality-check that rejects fallback if eval delta > configured threshold. Risks and trade-offs: - Aggressive shedding impacts customer experience; need careful canarying and per-customer exemptions. - Fallback to quantized models may introduce quality regressions; must guard with eval-set thresholds and rapid rollback hooks. - Active-active multi-region adds increased cost and replication complexity. Deliverables: 1) SLO declaration JSON schema + populated declarations for chat.generate, text.generate, embeddings and top 6 model variants. 2) Circuit breaker configuration and simulated behavior tests (load tests) for regional and global scopes. 3) Automated mitigation playbook and a feature-flagged controller implementation. 4) Dashboards and alert rules. 5) Runbooks and customer communication templates. Success criteria: - Automated mitigation controller handles simulated 3x burst without human intervention in >90% of test runs while maintaining critical-route SLOs. - Error budget alerting reduces manual paging frequency by 60% in the pilot. - No more than 3 customer-facing quality regressions in the 30d rollout window (tracked via eval set and customer tickets).
acceptance_criteria: Machine-readable SLO declarations committed to infra repo and validated by schema lint
Controller unit + integration tests covering burn-rate thresholds and circuit-breaker state transitions
Load-test report demonstrating controller prevents regional cascade in 90% of runs
Dashboards with burn-rate panels and circuit-breaker states in console, and alert rules wired to ops channels
Runbooks published and on-call trainings completed with checklist sign-off by runtime-sre and model-serving leads
